title: Spring JDBC reserves fresh IDs after a MySQL transaction failure
summary: After a confirmed rollback, the parent issued 100, 99, 100 and the third insert hit the primary key. The merge issued 99, 100, 101. After a real commit followed by a restoration failure, the merged retries began at 101 and ended with durable maximum 104.

change.description: The incrementer now discards the remaining cached IDs when commit or auto-commit restoration fails.

notes: A fresh MySQL 9.1.0 container runs the two InnoDB tables. Connector/J executes every query. A JDBC wrapper records the actual last_insert_id() read and injects one failure at the first commit or the first post-commit restoration. Each insert commits separately and every readback opens a new physical connection.
